Adventures with Grace

Crossing the Tropic of Cancer
Yunnan April Holiday Family Adventure 🌈

April 2027 school holidays · Xishuangbanna Water Festival · Primeval Forest Park · Tropic of Cancer · the mysterious Ailao Mountains · Dian Lake, Pearl of the Plateau

Head north from the rainforests of Xishuangbanna, cross the Tropic of Cancer in Mojiang and finish in Kunming, the City of Eternal Spring 🧭
Take the kids to a real Dai New Year Water-Splashing Festival in Xishuangbanna, China. No need to fight over water pistols: the whole city is the battlefield, and the wetter you get, the more blessings you receive 💦
Trek through the Jinuo Mountain rainforest, wading up streams and swinging on vines; be little farmers in Mojiang, picking tea, catching fish and planting rice, and make friends at a local high school; then walk into the misty old-growth forest of the Ailao Mountains and see Huayao Dai embroidery. We finish in Kunming with the Stone Forest, a hot spring, grass sledding, laser tag and Asia’s biggest flower market 🌺

📌 The itinerary may change slightly depending on flights, weather and local conditions; the final version will be confirmed before departure.

🇨🇳 Friends coming from within China are welcome to meet us in Kunming.

Trip details

Registrations open

🌈 Crossing the Tropic of Cancer: Yunnan April Holiday Family Adventure

Kids: here to get soaked and muddy. Water fights, tea picking, fishing, rice planting, and a few new friends in Yunnan.
Parents: here to watch them have the time of their lives. Routes, trains and drivers are all sorted, so you just take the photos 📸

DatesDepart Saturday 10 April 2027 (evening)
Back in Sydney Tuesday 27 April (morning)
During the NSW autumn school holidays (public schools return 29 April)
Exact times depend on flights and the group fare
RouteKunming → Xishuangbanna → Mojiang → Ailao Mountains (Gasa) → Kunming
Group4–5 families
Getting aroundBullet trains between cities (Kunming to Xishuangbanna is only 3.5 hours); private bus on the expressway from Mojiang to the Ailao Mountains and back to Kunming. Xishuangbanna and Kunming are arranged by Grace’s old classmate, who runs a travel agency there; Grace arranges Mojiang with local contacts
What kind of tripNot a tour – a few families exploring together
Local feasts along the way, plus some free meals to eat what you like 🍽️
No compulsory shopping stops; anyone keen on gold, silver or jade can visit a reputable shop if they wish
Everything at cost; Grace charges no fee
🗓️ Itinerary
  • Sat 10 Apr Evening departure from Sydney, changing planes in Shanghai ✈️
  • Sun 11 Apr Afternoon arrival in Kunming; one night there
    🍽️ Crossing-the-bridge rice noodles – our first taste of Yunnan
  • Mon 12 Apr Early train to Xishuangbanna; we stay near Gaozhuang
    🍽️ Free evening: graze your way around the Gaozhuang night market – leaf-wrapped grilled meats, bamboo-tube rice, pineapple rice
  • Tue 13 Apr Festival day one: afternoon riverside market, dragon-boat races and bamboo rockets, then thousands of sky lanterns and river lanterns at night 🏮
    🍽️ Dai home cooking
  • Wed 14 Apr Menglun Tropical Botanical Garden – China’s largest, with nearly 10,000 tropical plants in palm, banyan and dragon-blood-tree gardens 🌴 Afternoon at the Primeval Forest Park: peacocks taking flight 🦚, a waterfall, an Aini village and ethnic dances, plus a jungle zipline for the brave. At dusk, dress up in Dai clothes for photos at the Golden Pagoda
    🍽️ Peacock Feast: a Dai banquet laid out on banana leaves like a peacock’s tail – lemongrass fish, Dai roast chicken, purple rice (no peacocks involved 😄)
  • Thu 15 Apr Festival day: the river water-collecting and Buddha-bathing ceremonies in the morning, then the whole city gets splashed 💦 Afternoon at the Dai Ethnic Garden for a village-style water fight
    🍽️ Home-style Dai lunch after the splashing
  • Fri 16 Apr Jinuo Mountain rainforest trek: 4.5 km of wading up streams and rock-hopping across rivers, with a guide clearing the way with a machete and pointing out rainforest creatures such as giant orb spiders and firefly larvae 🌿 Swing on vines above the stream, drink water from a jungle vine and try banana-stem snacks
    🍽️ Rainforest feast: soup in bamboo cups and dishes on banana leaves – ants, flowers and dew for the brave 🐜
  • Sat 17 Apr Early train to Mojiang; afternoon spring tea picking and fishing in a muddy pond 🐟
    🍽️ Hani village feast: Mojiang purple rice, plus the fish we caught that day
  • Sun 18 Apr Rice planting; a costume workshop to see embroidery, batik and tie-dye, and tie-dye your own handkerchief 🎨; the Tropic of Cancer park, with its rainbow “flying carpet” slide and planetarium ☀️
    🍽️ Twins Feast, a local specialty of the “City of Twins”
  • Mon 19 Apr Morning visit to a local high school (see below) 🤝 Afternoon private bus on the expressway to Gasa, at the foot of the Ailao Mountains (about 2 hours)
    🍽️ Free evening meal
  • Tue 20 Apr Ailao Mountains: walk into misty old-growth forest draped in moss, like a fairy tale 🌲 See a waterfall, visit a Huayao Dai village and their heritage embroidery
    🍽️ Huayao Dai feast
  • Wed 21 Apr Morning at the Longxi family manor, then back to Kunming (about 3 hours)
    🍽️ Steam-pot chicken
  • Thu 22 Apr Old Kunming: Green Lake Park → Yunnan Military Academy (where future marshals Zhu De and Ye Jianying studied) → the former campus of Southwest Associated University, China’s famous wartime university → the old streets
    🍽️ Old Kunming street food: erkuai rice cakes and tofu-pudding rice noodles
  • Fri 23 Apr Western Hills, Dian Lake and Grand View Tower: the Dragon Gate cliff path in the morning, then Grand View Tower to see the “longest couplet in China” – 180 characters. Which kid can memorise it? 😄
    🍽️ Mushroom feast
  • Sat 24 Apr Stone Forest, then a night at a hot-spring hotel ♨️
    🍽️ Yiliang roast duck on the way
  • Sun 25 Apr Morning grass sledding and outdoor laser tag in the hills 🎯 (or the Yunnan Provincial Museum and similar for anyone who prefers) Dounan Flower Market in the evening 🌺
    🍽️ Flower Feast: dishes cooked with edible flowers – and flower cakes to take home
  • Mon 26 Apr Midday flight from Kunming via Shanghai
  • Tue 27 Apr Back in Sydney in the morning. NSW public schools return on Thursday 29 April, so there are two days to rest
  • The itinerary may change slightly depending on flights, weather and local conditions; the final version will be confirmed before departure
🌾 Mojiang: little farmers
  • Pick spring tea and see how leaves on a bush become tea in your cup 🍵
  • Catch fish in a muddy pond. Clothes won’t survive – bring a spare set 🐟
  • Plant rice in the paddies with local farmers (depending on the season)
  • Visit a local costume workshop to see how Hani clothing is made – embroidery, batik and tie-dye. Kids can tie-dye their own handkerchief to take home 🎨
  • Mojiang is a Hani autonomous county, so kids can buy traditional Hani clothes and wear them around the village 👗
  • Tropic of Cancer park: stand right on the line for a photo, ride the rainbow “flying carpet” slide down the hill and visit the planetarium ☀️
  • Make friends and learn from each other at a local high school: our kids teach English, they teach Chinese; play table tennis, soccer and basketball together 🏓⚽🏀, chess and calligraphy, and Rubik’s cube fans can show others a few tricks 🧩
  • Grace has already been in touch with the Mojiang tourism bureau. This trip is a first look: the plan is to grow Mojiang into a longer rural and school exchange, and you’ll be the very first families to try it 🌟
🌲 Ailao Mountains: misty old-growth forest
  • A national nature reserve with ancient moss-covered forest, often wrapped in cloud – like stepping into a fairy tale
  • Gasa and Mosha, in the Red River valley below, are home to the Huayao (Flowery Waist) Dai: heritage embroidery and authentic Dai food
  • A waterfall and the century-old Longxi family manor
  • We take the expressway from Mojiang and back to Kunming – no winding mountain roads
💰 Estimated costs (per person)
  • Return flights (group fare): about $1,000–1,500
  • Local costs (trains, buses, guide, hotels, feasts and entry tickets): pending the local quote, shared at cost
  • Free-time meals and personal shopping are your own
  • These are estimates; final figures will be shared in the group chat
📋 Before you go
  • Passports must be valid for at least 6 months; we need passport details to book the group fare
  • Australian passport holders can currently visit China visa-free – please check the latest rules before departure
  • Each family should take out travel insurance
  • Xishuangbanna is hot in April, so bring sunscreen and a hat; Kunming is cool in the mornings and evenings, so pack a jacket
  • Water Festival essentials: a waterproof phone pouch, sandals and at least two changes of clothes
  • The festival is very crowded. Please give each child a wristband with a parent’s phone number. Parents look after their own children

How to join

  1. 1. Tell us who’s coming

    Message Grace on WhatsApp or WeChat (leigracezhang) with the number of adults and children, and the children’s ages.

  2. 2. Pay a deposit to secure your spot

    Group flights must be reserved early, so a deposit is required. Your spot is confirmed once the deposit is paid, on a first-paid, first-served basis.
    · Deposit: $300 per person (to hold the group flights)
    · Balance: due before the group tickets are issued; we’ll confirm the date
    Payment: PayID transfer (Grace’s mobile number). If you don’t have it, message Grace on WeChat: leigracezhang.

  3. 3. Refunds

    The deposit and balance are non-refundable unless the trip is cancelled due to circumstances beyond our control (such as flight cancellations, a pandemic or a natural disaster). If you can’t make it for personal or family reasons, let Grace know as soon as possible and we’ll help you find someone to take your place.
